claim.pdf_says: In the 14.9.20.2 general format the underlines mark exactly these words as required: INITIALIZE, FILLER, ALL, VALUE, REPLACING, BY, DEFAULT. The words WITH, TO, THEN and DATA are printed WITHOUT underlines and are therefore optional words — so `INITIALIZE X FILLER`, `INITIALIZE X ALL VALUE`, `INITIALIZE X REPLACING NUMERIC BY 0` and `INITIALIZE X DEFAULT` are all legal.
claim.markdown_says: A fenced code block containing `INITIALIZE { identifier-1 } ... [ WITH FILLER ]`, `⎢ ⎨ ⎩ TO VALUE ⎥`, `⎢ THEN REPLACING ⎨ category-name DATA BY ⎨ ⎬ ⎬ ...⎥` and `[ THEN TO DEFAULT ]` — with no underlining and no figure note attached.
claim.why_it_matters: The code block carries no underlining and, unlike the `where category-name is:` figure immediately below it on the same page (which DOES get a note ending "Every one of the thirteen words is underlined (required word) in the printed figure"), this figure gets no compensating note. The required/optional split is therefore unrecoverable for five word pairs — WITH/FILLER, TO/VALUE, THEN/REPLACING, DATA/BY and THEN TO/DEFAULT. The failure mode is the falsely-restrictive one: an implementation built from this text requires WITH, TO, THEN and DATA and rejects legal source.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently verified against a 300 dpi render of PDF page 667 (printed folio 637) and against the live specs/ISO_COBOL.md at lines 27522-27575.

GLYPHS I ACTUALLY SEE IN THE PRINTED FIGURE (each checked at 3x-4x magnification, not from OCR):
  * Line 1 `INITIALIZE { identifier-1 } ... [ WITH FILLER ]` — a rule runs the full width of INITIALIZE and a separate rule runs the full width of FILLER. WITH has clear white space beneath it, flanked on both sides by the two rules; there is no rule under it. `identifier-1` is not underlined.
  * Line 2 `{ ALL / category-name } TO VALUE` — rule under ALL, rule under VALUE, nothing under TO, nothing under category-name. The gap between the end of the ALL/VALUE rules and TO is unambiguous at this zoom.
  * Line 3 `THEN REPLACING { category-name DATA BY { identifier-2 / literal-1 } } ...` — a long rule spans REPLACING only; THEN sits on bare paper. A short rule sits under BY only; I cropped `category-name DATA BY` at ~4x specifically to test for a faint DATA rule and there is none — the baseline under D-A-T-A is clean white, and the rule begins under the B of BY and ends under the Y.
  * Line 4 `[ THEN TO DEFAULT ]` — one rule, starting under the D of DEFAULT. THEN and TO are both bare.
So the claim's enumeration is exactly right: required = INITIALIZE, FILLER, ALL, VALUE, REPLACING, BY, DEFAULT; optional = WITH, TO, THEN, DATA.

PER THE STANDARD'S OWN CONVENTION, that distinction is normative content, not typography. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 2628: "Keywords ... are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required..."; line 2641: "Optional words ... are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats"; line 5805: "uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format." Dropping the underlines therefore drops the required/optional bit for four distinct reserved words at five sites, and the four sample statements the claim lists (`INITIALIZE X FILLER`, `INITIALIZE X ALL VALUE`, `INITIALIZE X REPLACING NUMERIC BY 0`, `INITIALIZE X DEFAULT`) are all legal COBOL that the markdown text alone gives no way to derive.

I TRIED HARD TO REFUTE THIS AND COULD NOT:
  (a) Not reflow/wrapping/furniture. Every word is present in the markdown and in the right order; the defect is the loss of a per-word attribute, which no amount of re-reading the code block recovers.
  (b) Not a blanket transcription convention that would make the omission harmless or systemic-by-design. The transcription's established convention is the opposite: it records underlining in a `> **Figure notes ...**` block, and does so in ~40+ places I sampled (e.g. lines 3920, 3964, 4101, 4315, 4547, 4871, 6178-6216, 6463-6526, 6588, 6826, 7059), routinely calling out which words are **not** underlined — "`FORMAT` and `IS` are **not** underlined — they are optional words" (line 4871), "`ALL` is **not** underlined — it is an optional word" (6178). By its own convention this figure is missing its note.
  (c) Not recoverable from an adjacent note. The immediately following `where category-name is:` figure DOES carry a note (line 27570) that ends "Every one of the thirteen words is underlined (required word) in the printed figure" — verified accurate against the render, all thirteen category names are ruled. That note covers only the second figure, and its existence makes the asymmetry sharper, exactly as the claim states.
  (d) Not recoverable from the surrounding prose. 14.9.20.3 syntax rules and 14.9.20.4 general rules (read through line 27609) name the phrases ("the REPLACING phrase", "the VALUE phrase") but never state that WITH/TO/THEN/DATA may be omitted.

MATERIAL HARM IS ALREADY REALIZED IN THIS REPO, which settles the severity question. src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:558-583 encodes `(WITH? FILLER)?`, `THEN? REPLACING`, and `initializeCategory DATA? BY` — correct — but line 567 is `(ALL | initializeCategory)? TO VALUE` and line 578 is `THEN? TO DEFAULT`, i.e. TO is mandatory in both places. TO is not underlined at either site in the printed figure, so `INITIALIZE X ALL VALUE` and `INITIALIZE X DEFAULT` are legal source the compiler currently rejects. That is precisely the falsely-restrictive failure mode the claim predicts, produced by exactly the two sites where the markdown lost the information.
verdict.corrected_description:
CONFIRMED, with two small refinements to the wording.

(1) Taxonomy. The figure's *text* is transcribed correctly — words, brackets, braces, and ellipses all match the print. What is missing is the underline (required-word) annotation and the compensating `Figure notes` block that the transcription applies to comparable figures elsewhere. "incorrect-figure" is defensible but "figure missing its required-word / underline note" is the precise defect; the fix is to append a note to specs/ISO_COBOL.md after line 27550 rather than to alter the code block's characters.

(2) Count. It is five *sites* but four distinct optional words: WITH (before FILLER), TO (before VALUE), THEN (before REPLACING), DATA (before BY), and THEN + TO (before DEFAULT) — TO and THEN each appear twice. Required words are INITIALIZE, FILLER, ALL, VALUE, REPLACING, BY, DEFAULT; `identifier-1`, `identifier-2`, `literal-1` and `category-name` are lowercase metavariables and unaffected.

Suggested note text: "**Figure notes (14.9.20.2 general format).** INITIALIZE, FILLER, ALL, VALUE, REPLACING, BY and DEFAULT are underlined in the printed standard (required words). WITH, TO (in both `TO VALUE` and `THEN TO DEFAULT`), THEN (in both `THEN REPLACING` and `THEN TO DEFAULT`) and DATA are printed **without** underlines — they are optional words per 8.3.1.1.2 and may be omitted. Hence `INITIALIZE X FILLER`, `INITIALIZE X ALL VALUE`, `INITIALIZE X REPLACING NUMERIC BY 0` and `INITIALIZE X DEFAULT` are all legal."

Actionable follow-up beyond the transcription: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4 lines 567 and 578 make TO mandatory and must become optional (`(ALL | initializeCategory)? TO? VALUE` and `THEN? TO? DEFAULT`), with an edition-gate sweep and goldens covering `INITIALIZE X ALL VALUE` and `INITIALIZE X DEFAULT`.
